reason: README documents tools/infer.py inference with pretrained PP-PicoDet weights, which runs on CPU with small downloads.
demo: Quick start / getting started: python tools/infer.py -c configs/picodet/picodet_s_320_coco_lcnet.yml -o weights=https://paddledet.bj.bcebos.com/models/picodet_s_320_coco_lcnet.pdparams --infer_img=demo/000000014439.jpg
goal: Get PaddleDetection object detection inference working on CPU. Run tools/infer.py with configs/picodet/picodet_s_320_coco_lcnet.yml, the pretrained picodet_s_320_coco_lcnet weights from paddledet.bj.bcebos.com, on the bundled demo/000000014439.jpg with use_gpu=False, and save the visualized result to an output directory.
check: The hidden test runs the detection on a bundled demo image on CPU and verifies a visualized output image is produced and detections were reported.

revision.by: second review (outside the maintained set; independent log check of maintained passes)
issues: Too lenient: the 'detections were reported' check is `grep -qi "class_id\|score\|bbox"` on the log, which matches the line 'Detection bbox results save in <file>' that trainer.predict logs for every saved image even with zero detections; the image-size and cmp checks also pass for an image with no boxes (it is re-encoded at quality 95). A model with broken/random weights would pass.
v2 adds the documented --save_results=True flag and checks bbox.json: >=3 detections with score>=0.5, >=2 of them COCO person (id 1), boxes inside the 640x404 image.
Demo and goal are fine: tools/infer.py on the bundled demo image with the small official PP-PicoDet-S weights; use_gpu=False is the config switch for CPU.
evidence: src/paddlepaddle-paddledetection/ppdet/engine/trainer.py:1277 — logger.info('Detection bbox results save in {}') runs for every visualized image, independent of bbox_num
